images.title: Longest row wins
images.purpose: Show that when one smiley is one student, the longest row is the most students.
images.composition: Two horizontal rows of smileys stacked with wide space between them, the key small above, one note centred below.
images.exact_structure: Key at top: 1 smiley = 1 student. Row 1: exactly 4 amber #E69F00 smileys, labelled Private car 4. Row 2: exactly 11 teal #0072B2 smileys of the same size and evenly spaced, labelled School bus 11, clearly longer. Rows start at the same left edge. Exactly 2 rows, 15 smileys in all.
labels: Longest row is the most students
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
rows of different smiley sizes or uneven spacing
images.takeaway: The longest row shows the most students.
images.description: Two rows of smileys: 4 amber for private car and 11 teal for school bus, with the key 1 smiley = 1 student.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count each row and say which row is longest.

image_decisions.why: Reading the longest row of a first pictograph is a picture idea; two rows carry it cleanly.
